A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sum-of-Parts research by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and VOC experiments in Table 1 and quantitative analyses of cosmological group weights in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification, cosmology, faithfulness, purity, sensitivity, and human-study results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v1's generator uses sparsemax to produce continuous sparse masks. v2 instead thresholds softmax attention into binary groups retaining the top 20% of features. Appendix C.7 introduces attention-derived gradient-passing scales and different scaled objectives for classification and regression. These substantially change group generation and optimization, while retaining weighted aggregation of group predictions.

E1.justification: v1 restricts ImageNet evaluation to ten classes and includes VOC multilabel classification. v2 removes VOC, uses the broader ImageNet task and ImageNet-S annotations covering 919 classes, and adds human evaluation of explanations. CosmoGrid regression is retained and expanded into comparative evaluation; it is not a newly introduced dataset.

E2.justification: The six ImageNet comparators in v1 expand to fourteen in v2, adding FullGrad, Archipelago, MFABA, AGI, AMPE, BCos, XDNN, and BagNet. The main comparisons convert post-hoc methods into thresholded '-F' predictors rather than merely renaming them. CosmoGrid gains comparisons against ten converted methods; BCos, XDNN, BagNet, and FRESH are excluded there.

E3.justification: v2 replaces pixelwise and whole-group insertion/deletion with simultaneous group growth/shrinkage, normalized probability AUCs, and a penalty for incorrect deletion predictions. It adds fidelity, purity, and human-distinction protocols with 20% feature selection. ImageNet-S uses one validation example per class. Cosmological structure identification changes from mean-intensity criteria to pixel-fraction thresholds, preventing direct comparison of the resulting weights.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's cosmology case study and brief segmentation/threshold observations, v2 adds sparsity–error curves, purity–performance analyses, correct-versus-incorrect object/background analyses, cosmological threshold sensitivity, and finer insertion/deletion steps. Appendix C.8 also reports qualitative initialization, attention-head, and frozen-versus-finetuned encoder ablations. Figures 2 and 12–16 add comparative attribution examples.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without experimental uncertainty reporting. v2 adds ± quantities throughout its numerical comparison tables and human-study error bars, with standard deviations estimated using 1,000 bootstrap repetitions for the human study. Training-run counts, random seeds, and the interpretation of the other tables' ± quantities remain unspecified; increased training repetitions cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v1's ImageNet/VOC results are replaced by substantially different benchmark results, and v2 adds purity, fidelity, and human-study outcomes. These are not same-setting performance gains. Cosmological cluster weights change from 8.8% for Omega_m versus 14.8% for sigma_8 in v1 Section 5 to 34.0% versus 28.4% in v2 Figure 9, reversing their ordering under revised group and structure definitions.

T1.justification: The two principal exponential-error results change from v1 Theorems 2.3 and 2.5 to v2 Conjectures 1 and 2, substantially changing their asserted formal status, although retained prose still calls them proved. Appendix A corrects the binomial argument's S2-union-S2 term to S2-union-S3. v2 also introduces task-specific purity definitions. The grouped zero-error proof is largely retained and moved from the appendix, not newly established.

C1.justification: v2 expands the central claims from overcoming attribution-error barriers and improving most perturbation metrics to overcoming self-explaining models' performance–faithfulness trade-off. Its abstract and introduction add claims about highest comparative performance, semantic purity, and human usefulness. SOP is explicitly framed as converting differentiable pretrained models into self-explaining models, narrowing the earlier unrestricted backbone language.

C2.justification: v1 links high-significance clusters particularly to sigma_8; v2 interprets both voids and clusters as more informative for Omega_m. v2 adds explanations involving binary-mask information leakage, adaptive attention during deletion, and object/background associations with errors. It also explicitly discusses differentiability, training overhead, sparsity-dependent accuracy limitations, and the human study's inability to establish a clearly superior method.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents frozen backbone components, embedding initialization, group limits, optimizer settings, one-epoch training, learning rate 5e-6, absent warmup, GPU models, and training/evaluation times. Appendices B–C provide substantially fuller implementation and human-study instructions. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. The advertised code address changes from DebugML/sop to BrachioLab/sop; both versions already claim code availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions SOP within self-explaining models, explicitly relating it to Alvarez Melis and Jaakkola's framework and expanding discussion of grouped attributions, concept bottlenecks, explanation evaluation, and human utility. It adds numerous relevant works and a detailed comparison with Bilodeau et al. Publication updates to retained works are distinct from these substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, evaluation narrative, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces a separate self-explaining-model section and organizes performance and utility around six research questions. Much of v1's cosmology background moves to Appendix D.3, while grouped-error definitions and their proof move into the main text.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and relocates the pipeline diagram, replaces the original group-to-class illustration with comparative attribution displays, and restructures the main results table. It adds trade-off plots, error-analysis charts, human-study displays, and appendix example grids. Cosmology histograms change from four separate panels to two overlaid comparisons. The exponential-error plots are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited direct validation of semantic quality and human usefulness through purity measurements, error analyses, broader image coverage, and a human study with explicit uncertainty qualifications. Its implementation and optimization documentation also makes the work considerably more assessable. VOC coverage is lost, and changed AUC protocols prevent same-setting performance claims. Remaining conjecture/proof inconsistencies and undefined general uncertainty labels limit the gains, but the improvements to validation and reproducibility are substantial.
